Before I build this, one honest flag: we don't have verified ROI benchmarks or an average cost-per-activation number yet. Those are exactly the kind of specific stats the brand guardrails require to come from real data, not invented ones, so I'm not going to fabricate them. What I can do instead is build a guide that gives sponsoring organizations something more useful right now: a planning framework they fill in with their own numbers, plus the real, sourced engagement stats we do have, and a clear picture of what verified reporting will look like once they're live. That earns the opt-in without overpromising, and it sets up the ROI conversation honestly.

Here's the lead magnet.

## 1. Five concept options

**1. "Funded Capacity Planning Guide"** (worksheet)
What they get: A budget and participation planning tool for standing up an acknowledgment program, with fields for their own cost assumptions instead of invented averages.
Why it earns the email: Finance and HR leads need a planning tool before they'll bring this to a budget conversation.
Path: Guide → sponsor onboarding call → pilot proposal.

**2. "The Sponsor's Guide to Funded Capacity"** (guide)
What they get: A plain-language walkthrough of how funding, activation, delivery, and verification work from a sponsor's seat.
Why it earns the email: Decision-makers want to understand the model before they'll talk numbers.
Path: Guide → welcome sequence → discovery call.

**3. "Is Your Organization Ready to Sponsor Gratitude?"** (checklist)
What they get: A self-assessment to see if their org has the right conditions (headcount, budget cycle, existing recognition spend) to launch.
Why it earns the email: Fast to consume, easy first step for a cautious buyer.
Path: Checklist → qualification email → sales conversation.

**4. "Employee Acknowledgment That Delivers"** (playbook)
What they get: A step-by-step launch plan from first funded capacity to first verified activation.
Why it earns the email: Appeals to HR/People teams who need an implementation plan, not just philosophy.
Path: Playbook → onboarding sequence → pilot.

**5. "Beyond Recognition Software"** (comparison guide)
What they get: A framework comparing funded, verified acts to point-and-badge recognition platforms.
Why it earns the email: Useful for orgs currently evaluating Workhuman, Achievers, or similar tools.
Path: Guide → competitive follow-up email → demo.

Given what you asked for, I built out **Concept 1**, reframed honestly around planning inputs rather than invented benchmarks.

---

## 2. Full lead magnet content

```markdown
# Funded Capacity Planning Guide
### A worksheet for sponsoring organizations building an employee acknowledgment program

## Why this exists

Most recognition programs run on points, badges, and budget lines nobody can connect to a real outcome. Gratitude.com works differently: your organization funds real-world acts in advance, your people activate them, a trusted nonprofit partner delivers, and delivery is verified. You see what your funding made possible, not just what it cost.

This guide helps you plan that program before you launch it: how much capacity to fund, how participation typically works, and what you'll see in reporting.

## The problem this solves

Recognition gets lost more often than most organizations realize:

- 60% of people never or rarely express gratitude to their coworkers, and 74% never or rarely express it to their boss. (John Templeton Foundation Gratitude Survey, Penn Schoen Berland)
- 82% of employees say recognition matters to them, yet most go years without one meaningful acknowledgment. (SurveyMonkey)

The gap isn't good intention. It's the absence of a system that turns intention into something real.

## How sponsoring works

- **You fund capacity.** Your organization creates funded, ready-to-activate acts for your employees, customers, or community. This can be one-time or recurring.
- **Your people activate.** They choose an available act. It costs them nothing at the moment because the capacity already exists.
- **A trusted nonprofit partner delivers it.** Delivery is confirmed rather than assumed.
- **You see what happened.** Verified outcomes come back to your organization, not just a confirmation that a budget line was spent.
- **Attribution stays subtle.** If you want it, "Made possible by [Your Organization]" appears. Your brand never overpowers the act or the person choosing it.

## Planning your capacity: fill this in with your own numbers

We are not going to hand you an industry-average cost per activation or a projected ROI multiple. Those figures depend on the specific acts you fund, your partner mix, and your population size, and we would rather help you plan with real inputs than a borrowed average. Use this worksheet with your own budget and headcount:

| Planning input | Your number |
|---|---|
| Number of employees, customers, or community members eligible to activate | |
| Target participation rate for your first quarter | |
| Budget allocated to funded capacity (one-time or recurring) | |
| Preferred cadence (one-time launch, monthly, quarterly) | |
| Acts or causes most relevant to your people (if known) | |
| Internal owner for this program | |

Once you have these filled in, we can help you translate them into a specific capacity plan and a realistic launch size. [Specific cost-per-act and ROI benchmarks will be shared during onboarding as pilot data becomes available. NEEDS INPUT until then.]

## What you'll see in reporting

- Which acts were activated and by how many people
- Confirmation that a trusted nonprofit partner delivered each one
- Verified status, not self-reported completion
- The kind of result your funding created, shared in a way that respects the privacy and dignity of everyone involved

## Your next step

Fill in the worksheet above with your own numbers. Then talk to us about turning it into a funded capacity plan sized to your organization.
```

---

## 3. Opt-in page copy

**Headline:** Plan Your Organization's Acknowledgment Program Before You Launch It

- See exactly how funded capacity, activation, and verified delivery work for sponsors
- Use our planning worksheet to size your budget and participation goals with your own numbers
- Understand what you'll see in reporting before your first employee ever activates an act

---

## 4. Delivery email

**Subject: Your Funded Capacity Planning Guide**

Here's the guide.

It walks through how sponsoring works at Gratitude.com: you fund real-world acts in advance, your people activate them at no cost to themselves, a trusted nonprofit partner delivers, and you see verified results.

Inside, you'll find a short worksheet to size your program using your own headcount and budget. We didn't fill it in with industry averages. Cost per activation and ROI vary by the acts you fund and the population you're serving, and we'd rather help you plan with real numbers than a borrowed one.

Once you've filled it in, reply to this email and we'll help you turn it into a capacity plan sized to your organization.

Michael Hilf
Founder & CEO, Gratitude.com

Tell me if you want the welcome sequence that follows this delivery email, or a designed PDF version of the guide, and I'll build it next.

grade.reasons: Correctly refuses to invent ROI benchmarks or cost per activation, flags them as NEEDS INPUT, and still delivers a complete usable structure (concepts, full guide, opt-in copy, delivery email) with a clear next step. Voice is warm, direct, uses locked vocabulary (fund/activate, trusted nonprofit partner, verified), no em dashes, no hype, and subtle sponsor attribution done right. Facts are limited to the two sourced stats and no guaranteed ROI is promised; the '[NEEDS INPUT]' placeholder is embedded honestly.
